stem.text: Let \( g(x) = - 2 x^{3} + 12 x^{2} - 18 x - 3 \). Using the second derivative test where it applies, determine whether g has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at \( x = 1 \) and at \( x = -5 \).

answer_key.label: At \( x = 1 \), g has a relative minimum because \( g'(1) = 0 \) and \( g''(1) = 12 > 0 \); at \( x = -5 \), g has no relative extremum because \( g'(-5) = -288 \ne 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate: \( g'(x) = - 6 x^{2} + 24 x - 18 \), which factors as \( g'(x) = - 6 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x - 1\right) \).
\( g'(1) = 0 \), so \( x = 1 \) is a critical point, while \( g'(-5) = -288 \ne 0 \), so \( x = -5 \) is not.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points are zeros of the first derivative
second derivative evaluated at the critical point

worked_solution.text: By the second derivative test g has a relative minimum at \( x = 1 \). At \( x = -5 \) the first derivative is not zero, so g has no relative extremum there and the test does not apply.

options.derivation: the relative extremum from the second derivative test extended to an absolute one with no argument that it is the only critical point, which it is not
